sentences.text:
Writ Petition No.13393 of 2019
O R D E R:

This writ petition is filed by the petitioner, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, with the following relief:
"..... to issue a Writ of Mandamus, or other appropriate writ, order or direction,
d e c l a r i n g a c t i o n o f t h e 5 t h r e s p o n d e n t i n c o n t i n u i n g t h e c a s e No.006/D1/KR/05222/2015 and case No.006/D1/KR/05223/2015 though the petitioner was prosecuted and acquitted in C.C.No.308 of 2016 and C.C.No.813 of 2016 on the file of the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Vijayawada with regard to same inspection dated 27.10.2015 and subsequent inspection dated 04.12.2015 respectively as illegal, arbitrary, barred under the principles of 'double jeopardy', violative of Articles 14, 20 and 21 of the Constitution of India, violative of principles of natural justice and contrary to the provisions of the Food Safety and S t a n d a r d s A c t , 2 0 0 6 a n d c o n s e q u e n t l y s e t a s i d e t h e c a s e No.006/D1/KR/05222/2015 and case No.006/D1/KR/05223/2015 pending before the 5th respondent....."
2) Heard, Sri Y.N. Anjaneyacharyulu, learned counsel for the petitioner who argued that his client is being prosecuted twice for the same offence.
Learned Government Pleader for Medical and Health appearing for respondents sought time to get instructions.
3) Learned counsel for the petitioner, however, requested to dispose of the writ petition on its own merits.
Learned Government Pleader opposes the same stating that parallel proceedings can continue and that the law on the subject is very clear.
He submits that 5th respondent can impose penalty.

It is also the contention of the learned Government Pleader that the standard of proof and the quality of evidence in these two proceedings are different, and, therefore, 'double jeopardy, etc.,
will not apply and that the acquittal in the criminal case will not bar the respondent No.5 from entertaining or disposing the case before him.

4) At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioner states that in these circumstances, 5th respondent may be directed to dispose of the complaint case No.006/D1/KR/05222/2015 and case No.006/D1/KR/05223/2015 that is pending before him.

5) Considering the submissions made, the 5th respondent is directed to hear and dispose of the matter on its own merits without in any way being influenced by this Court order, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of this order.
